cases.sentence: Я остался на ___, в полном одиночестве и полном недоумении.
cases.translation: I stayed on the vestibule platform, in complete solitude and complete bewilderment.
cases.explain: «На» answering «где?» (a static location, not motion towards) takes the prepositional: на площадке.

cases.translation: I pressed my head to the little window.
cases.explain: The preposition «к» (towards, up against) always governs the dative, so окошко becomes окошку.

cases.sentence: Я сразу понял, кто стоит у меня за ___.
cases.translation: I understood at once who was standing behind my back.
cases.explain: «За» meaning 'behind' with no movement involved takes the instrumental: за спиной.
It is the direct object of the transitive verb «смири»; порыв is inanimate, so its accusative looks like the nominative.

cases.sentence: Возьми – и на ходу из ___ выпрыгни.
cases.translation: Go on and jump out of the commuter train while it is moving.
cases.explain: «Из» (out of) always requires the genitive: из электрички.

cases.translation: And Satan went away, put to shame.
cases.explain: The word is the subject of the verb «ушел», and subjects stand in the nominative — even though Сатана has a feminine-looking ending.

cases.sentence: От Москвы до ___ ехать ровно два часа пятнадцать минут.
cases.translation: From Moscow to Petushki the journey takes exactly two hours and fifteen minutes.
cases.explain: «До» marking the end point of a distance governs the genitive; Петушки is plural, so the genitive is Петушков.

cases.sentence: Тьма сменяется ___, а свет сменяется тьмой.
cases.translation: Darkness gives way to light, and light gives way to darkness.
cases.explain: The verb «сменяться» (to be replaced by) takes its complement in the instrumental: сменяется светом.

reading.ru: Я остался на площадке, в полном одиночестве и полном недоумении.
reading.question: Where is Venichka at the start of the chapter?
options: Alone on the vestibule platform of the carriage
Asleep on a bench in the carriage
On the platform at Petushki station
reading.correct: Alone on the vestibule platform of the carriage
reading.explain: After the others leave he is left standing in the tambour, alone and bewildered.

reading.ru: Почему за окном чернота, если поезд вышел утром и прошел ровно сто километров?..
reading.question: What is Venichka unable to explain to himself?
options: Why it is pitch dark outside although the train left in the morning
Why the train has stopped between stations
Why his suitcase has gone missing
reading.correct: Why it is pitch dark outside although the train left in the morning
reading.explain: The train set off in the morning and has covered only a hundred kilometres, yet the window is black.

reading.ru: Я сразу понял, кто стоит у меня за спиной.
reading.question: Who comes up behind Venichka in the vestibule?
options: The old woman with the bundle
reading.explain: He recognises the gloating voice without even turning round, and the speaker is named as Satan.

reading.ru: Смири свой духовный порыв – легче будет.
reading.question: What is Satan's first piece of advice?
options: To humble his spiritual impulse so that things get easier
To have another drink at once
To go back and sit in the carriage
To get off at the next station
reading.correct: To humble his spiritual impulse so that things get easier
reading.explain: Satan argues that if it is hard for him, he should subdue his impulse and feel relief.

reading.question: How does Venichka answer that first piece of advice?
options: He refuses flatly to humble anything
He asks Satan for time to think it over
He pretends not to have heard
reading.correct: He refuses flatly to humble anything
reading.explain: His reply is a point-blank refusal, which earns him the exchange of insults that follows.

reading.ru: Не-а, не буду я прыгать, страшно.
reading.question: Why does Venichka turn down Satan's suggestion to jump from the moving train?
options: He is frightened and certain he would smash himself up
He has already tried it once before
He does not want to leave his suitcase behind
He is afraid of being fined
reading.correct: He is frightened and certain he would smash himself up
reading.explain: He thinks it over and says it is frightening and that he would be bound to smash himself.

reading.question: How does the encounter with Satan end?
options: Satan stays and drinks with him
Satan pushes him out of the door
Satan follows him into the carriage
reading.explain: Both temptations fail, and Satan withdraws put to shame.

reading.ru: Чернота все плыла за окном и все тревожила.
reading.question: What effect does the blackness outside the window keep having on Venichka?
options: It floats past and keeps troubling him
It sends him straight to sleep
reading.correct: It floats past and keeps troubling him
reading.explain: The darkness drifts past the glass, disturbs him and stirs up a black thought.

reading.ru: Тьма сменяется светом, а свет сменяется тьмой – таково мое мнение.
reading.question: What does the voice of his heart say about darkness and light?
options: That they simply replace one another and nothing can be done about it
That light always wins in the end
That darkness is a sign of misfortune
That only drunkards notice the difference
reading.correct: That they simply replace one another and nothing can be done about it
reading.explain: The heart argues that darkness is darkness, it alternates with light, and disliking it changes nothing.

reading.ru: Значит, остается один выход: принять эту тьму.
reading.question: What single way out does that argument arrive at?
options: To wake up the other passengers
reading.explain: Since the eternal laws of being cannot be beaten, the only option left is to accept the dark.

reading.ru: Зажав левую ноздрю, мы можем сморкнуться только правой ноздрей.
reading.question: Which homely image is used to show how little fools can do against the laws of being?
options: Holding one nostril shut, you can only blow your nose through the other
Beer spilt on a table cannot be gathered up again
A train cannot pass a post without stopping
An autumn day cannot be made longer by wishing
reading.correct: Holding one nostril shut, you can only blow your nose through the other
reading.explain: The nostril image illustrates that we fools cannot overcome the eternal laws of existence.

reading.ru: От Москвы до Петушков ехать ровно два часа пятнадцать минут.
reading.question: How long does the journey from Moscow to Petushki normally take?
options: Exactly two hours and fifteen minutes
Exactly one hour and ten minutes
reading.correct: Exactly two hours and fifteen minutes
reading.explain: He cites the normal running time to prove that it cannot possibly be night yet.

reading.ru: У каждого столба останавливается и стоит, а зачем стоит?
reading.question: What complaint is made about the way trains run nowadays?
options: The train stops at every post and stands there for no reason
The train never stops where you need it to
The train sets off before the passengers are on board
reading.correct: The train stops at every post and stands there for no reason
reading.explain: The retort is that trains used to be faster and now halt pointlessly at every post — except at Esino.

reading.ru: Вся публика в вагоне, человек пять или шесть, дремали вниз головой, как грудные младенцы…
reading.question: What are the other passengers doing when Venichka comes back into the carriage?
options: Five or six of them are dozing with their heads down like babies
They are arguing loudly about the timetable
They are getting ready to get off
reading.correct: Five or six of them are dozing with their heads down like babies
reading.explain: The whole public in the carriage — five or six people — is asleep head-down like infants, and he almost dozes off too.

reading.ru: Но ведь в 11 утра она должна меня ждать!
reading.question: What suddenly makes Venichka jump up from the bench?
options: The thought that she is to be waiting for him at 11 in the morning
The thought that he has lost his money
The realisation that he has missed his station
reading.correct: The thought that she is to be waiting for him at 11 in the morning
reading.explain: She is due to wait for him at eleven, yet it is still dark, so he fears he will have to wait for dawn himself.

reading.ru: Ты обещал ей пурпур и лилии, а везешь триста грамм конфет „Василек“.
reading.question: What is Venichka actually bringing his beloved instead of what he promised?
reading.explain: He promised her purple and lilies but is carrying the same cheap sweets he has brought twelve times before.

highlight.question: Which sentence says what the feeling really was, rather than bewilderment?
sentences: Я остался на площадке, в полном одиночестве и полном недоумении.
Это было даже не совсем недоумение, это была все та же тревога, переходящая в горечь.
В конце концов, черт с ним, пусть «милая странница», пусть «старший лейтенант», – но почему за окном темно, скажите мне, пожалуйста?
Почему за окном чернота, если поезд вышел утром и прошел ровно сто километров?..
Почему?..
highlight.explain: The second sentence corrects the word 'bewilderment' and names the feeling as anxiety turning into bitterness.

highlight.question: Which sentence says that Venichka knew at once who was standing behind him?
sentences: – А! Это ты! – кто-то сказал у меня за спиной таким приятным голосом, таким злорадным, что я даже поворачиваться не стал.
Я сразу понял, кто стоит у меня за спиной.
«Искушать сейчас начнет, тупая морда! Нашел же ведь время – искушать!»
highlight.explain: The middle sentence states directly that he understood immediately who was there.

highlight.question: Which sentence compares Venichka's thought to beer spreading across a table?
sentences: А я – что мне оставалось? – я сделал из горлышка шесть глотков и снова припал головой к окошку.
Чернота все плыла за окном и все тревожила.
И будила черную мысль.
Я стискивал голову, чтобы отточить эту мысль, но она все никак не оттачивалась, а растекалась, как пиво по столу.
«Не нравится мне эта тьма за окном, очень не нравится».
highlight.explain: The fourth sentence says the thought would not sharpen but spread out like beer on a table.

highlight.question: Which sentence concludes that it must already be Friday today?
sentences: Впрочем, стоп!
Ведь я уезжал из Москвы – заря моей пятницы уже взошла.
Значит – уже сегодня пятница!
Почему же так темно за окном?..»
highlight.explain: The third sentence draws the conclusion that today is already Friday.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes what the other passengers in the carriage were doing?
sentences: Вот это меня уже совсем утешило.
Я ушел с площадки снова в вагон и сел на лавочку, стараясь не глядеть в окошко.
Вся публика в вагоне, человек пять или шесть, дремали вниз головой, как грудные младенцы…
Я чуть было тоже не задремал…
highlight.explain: The third sentence pictures the five or six passengers dozing head-down like infants.

highlight.question: Which sentence says that Venichka gave himself up to the stream once more?
sentences: Тут я совсем почти задремал.
Я уронил голову себе на плечо и до Петушков не хотел ее поднимать.
Я снова отдался потоку…
highlight.explain: The closing sentence of the chapter states that he surrendered to the stream again.
